messages:
IncidentBot: Pager — Critical: Orpheon (customer) VPC auth failing for production tenant. Error: downstream JWKS fetch failing; many 401s. Paging @alice_ramos on-call.

Alice Ramos: I’m on it. Has anyone confirmed customer impact scope? Which routes failing?

Bob Kim: Seeing spikes of 401s from the dedicated pool bound to Orpheon-tenant-prod. Roughly ~40% of requests failing over last 3 mins.

Sophia Chen: Logs show `jwks_fetch_error` with underlying `x509: certificate has expired` when we call the customer JWKS url. Looks like their JWKS endpoint now requires mTLS and the client cert we have to talk to them is expired.

Alice Ramos: Thanks. @Luca Marino, did we recently rotate any client certs for Orpheon in the VPC connector config? I don’t recall a scheduled rotation.

Luca Marino: I deployed a cert rotation play for a different tenant last week but not Orpheon. Checking the connector config now.

Luca Marino: Confirmed: the connector (identity-proxy-orpheon) is presenting `client-cert-orpheon.pem` that expired 2026-02-28. Looks like the customer rotated their server policy to require mTLS and our cert expired silently.

Alice Ramos: So their JWKS endpoint now rejects our TLS handshake -> we get no JWKS -> token verification fails -> 401s. Outline mitigation options: 1) Temporarily allow cached JWKS/skip-live-JWKS for Orpheon (short window), 2) Ask customer to relax mTLS or accept new cert quickly, 3) Upload new client cert to our connector.

Bob Kim: Option 3 is fastest if we have a fresh cert. Do we? Search vault.

Sophia Chen: I don’t see a newer Orpheon cert in Vault. Customer sent an updated cert to their AE last week but I don’t think we ever ingested it.

Tom Patel: I’m the AE on this account. Customer confirms they generated a replacement client cert earlier (they have fingerprint ABCD:1234). They thought we had it; I’ll upload the cert now to our secure intake and post the location.

Tom Patel: Uploaded to `secrets/orpheon/client-cert-2026-03-15.pem` and `secrets/orpheon/client-key-2026-03-15.pem` (ACL: infra-ops, oncall). Ping when ingested.

Infra Ops Bot: New secret received for path `secrets/orpheon/` by Tom Patel. Approvals required: infra-ops, alice_ramos.

Alice Ramos: Approving ingestion. Bob/Sophia, can you coordinate to apply the cert to identity-proxy-orpheon? This will cause a short TLS reconnect to their JWKS endpoint.

Bob Kim: Will do. Rolling update plan: deploy new cert to one connector instance (canary), then monitor JWKS fetch success; if green, roll remaining nodes. Canary window ~2 minutes.

Sophia Chen: Before we update, put a short-lived fallback to use cached JWKS for verification to reduce errors for the in-flight requests. I can flip the runtime flag for Orpheon to `use_cached_jwks=true`.

Alice Ramos: Go ahead Sophia. Keep the fallback for <= 10 minutes max. Add rule: only accept cached keys that match existing kid set and no new keys allowed.

Sophia Chen: Done. `runtime-config set tenants.orpheon.use_cached_jwks true --ttl 600 --mode strict`

Bob Kim: Canary started on connector node `ip-10-2-5-11`. Pushed `client-cert-2026-03-15.pem`. Logs:
```
[TLS] presenting cert fingerprint ABCD:1234
[JWKS] fetch ok 200 - 11 keys
```

Bob Kim: Canary shows JWKS fetch success and token verification passing for canary requests. Rolling to other nodes now.

Alice Ramos: Good. Tom, notify customer we’ll be applying their cert and may see a small window of 401s during the roll. Ask them to confirm the fingerprint matches.

Tom Patel: Notified Orpheon SRE. They confirmed fingerprint matches and asked us to proceed. Also asked if there’s anything they should change on their side — they will keep mTLS required.

Bob Kim: Rolling complete across all connector nodes. Observability: 401 rate dropped from 40% -> 2% within 120s. New error rate mostly from older cached sessions; those are expiring.

Sophia Chen: Turning off cached JWKS now to return to normal verification mode.

Sophia Chen: `runtime-config set tenants.orpheon.use_cached_jwks false`

Alice Ramos: Can we add a short-lived alert to detect similar expired cert issues proactively? Perhaps a health check on mTLS handshake to JWKS endpoint with cert expiry delta.

Luca Marino: Agreed. I’ll add a monitor that checks certificate validity for all external JWKS endpoints we call from connectors and alert when expiry < 14 days.

Alice Ramos: Excellent. Also we need a customer-facing communication and internal post-incident action items.

Tom Patel: Drafting a note for Orpheon: summary, mitigation, ask to confirm cert rotation process going forward. Will share in #customer-communications and send once reviewed.

Alice Ramos: Action items logged:
- A1: Luca — add cert expiry monitor for JWKS endpoints (P0) — assigned
- A2: Bob/Sophia — add playbook step to ingest customer certs into Vault and run a dry TLS handshake (P1)
- A3: Tom — send customer post-incident summary (P1)
- A4: Infra — ensure secret ACL audit for `secrets/orpheon` (P2)

Bob Kim: Noted. I’ll also add a small improvement to connector startup to fail-fast if cert expired, and emit a dedicated metric `connector.tls.client_cert.expired`.

Alice Ramos: Thanks everyone. Marking incident as mitigated. I’ll keep this thread open for further follow-ups until postmortem assigned.

Infra Ops Bot: Incident auto-note: mitigation in place; assigning support ticket #INC-987654 to Orpheon case. Please attach logs and timeline.

Alice Ramos: Attaching brief timeline to ticket and assigning postmortem to myself + Sophia + Luca. Will schedule RCA in 48 hrs.

Tom Patel: Customer acknowledged and appreciated the quick response. They asked for a weekly sync to avoid cert miscoordination.

Alice Ramos: Closing intermediate paging. If anything regresses, re-pager immediately. :white_check_mark:
